result.text:
At yesterday's meetup I asked Marc why he's never shipped an AI wrapper 😅

His two most profitable products have almost nothing to do with AI. Everyone else is chasing the AI hype. He just doesn't.

His answer had two parts.

1. he builds things he wants to use himself every day.

2. he asks what still won't be replaceable by AI in 5 or 10 years. His example was TrustMRR. Real buyers and real sellers who trust the place. An AI wrapper can die the day OpenAI ships one new feature. But nobody ships a feature that takes your buyers and sellers away.

So you pick the niche, and you don't chase whatever is hot this month. With AI there's a new hype almost every single month. You pick, and then you wait. The compounding only shows up years later. And if you don't actually love the thing, you won't stay long enough to see it.

There's a word going around in China right now, OPC, one person company. Everyone wants to build one, and with AI making everything fast and easy, everyone wants one that prints money fast.

Marc told us he wanted to build a social network early on, right after watching The Social Network. He wanted to get rich. Everyone starts there 🤪

We're both just normal people, zero followers, zero products, no idea how to get users. Honestly we still think about that last part every day.

If you're starting one of these, pick something you like and are already a bit good at. Ship one feature in your MVP. See if anyone wants it. If they do, stay on it and listen to the people using it.

Then go tell the story yourself and build your own flywheel.

I only build 2 types of startups now:

1) AI-proof in 10 years. My startup marketplace (TrustMRR) can be cloned with a prompt, but a network of 20K buyers can’t. Trust compounds over time.

2) Trends. Anything hot on tech Twitter this month. GEO, new AI models, it can be anything, as long as people are actively talking about it.

I also have a 3rd filter: I build products I’m curious about. Or, even better, products I use myself.

legacy.full_text: Great guide on using the X API via our new XMCP and Grok Build to build a structured knowledge system powered by X—unlocking great use cases like agentic research, realtime monitoring the situation, and an audience flywheel to improve as creators on X.

blocks.text: Your X account can now become a programmable intelligence system. Most people use X bookmarks as a graveyard. You see something useful, save it, and tell yourself you will come back later
But after hundreds or thousands of bookmarks, the valuable information becomes almost impossible to find again
That changes when you connect the X API to an AI agent such as Grok Build, Hermes Agent, Claude Code or another MCP-compatible tool
I connected my X account to Grok Build and gave it one simple instruction:
“Read all my bookmarks, summarize everything I have saved and tell me whether there is anything important inside”
The agent went through all of my bookmarks and turned a messy collection of saved posts into structured intelligence
It identified:
The topics I save most often
The accounts I bookmark most
Recurring themes across my research
Important ideas buried inside old posts
Content with clear potential to become future systems and projects
Patterns in what consistently captures my attention
Instead of manually opening all the posts, reading them again and taking notes, the agent processed the entire collection and gave me a clear picture of what I had been saving
This is where the X API becomes much more powerful than most people realize

Your bookmarks are not simply saved posts. They are a personal dataset containing your interests, research, ideas, inspiration and unfinished intentions. An AI agent can turn that dataset into something you can actually use
You can ask:
“Summarize everything I bookmarked this month”
“Find the most important AI research I saved”
“Group my bookmarks into coding, design, business and content ideas”
“Show me the posts I saved but never acted on”
“Turn my best bookmarks into a research report”
“Create ten original ideas based on the themes I have been studying”
“Build a searchable knowledge base from everything I have saved”
“Identify ideas appearing repeatedly across different authors”
The agent does not merely retrieve links. It can read the posts, compare them, identify relationships, extract the useful parts and turn scattered information into a usable body of knowledge
And bookmarks are only the beginning

The X API gives AI agents controlled access to a much broader part of the platform. Depending on the permissions you provide, an agent can work with posts, users, timelines, bookmarks, likes, lists, search, news and trends
That opens up an entirely new category of workflows
1. Real-time research
X is where information appears first - Basically a platform where news breaks out first
Product launches, breaking news, technical discoveries, company updates, government announcements and eyewitness reports can begin circulating on X long before they become polished articles elsewhere
An agent connected to the X API can search that stream programmatically
You could ask it to:
Monitor selected accounts for important updates
Search for posts mentioning a company, product or topic
Track conversations around an unfolding event
Separate primary sources from commentary
Collect posts from verified employees or officials
Compare how a story develops over several hours
Produce a daily briefing from specific communities
Alert you when a meaningful new development appears

Instead of repeatedly refreshing feeds and opening dozens of tabs, your agent can perform the monitoring and return only what matters

Your agent can also watch official company channels for the updates you care about most stock moves, AI product launches, roadmap changes, delays or postponements and only alert you when something truly important happens.
2. A personal content engine
For creators, the X API can turn an AI agent into a complete research and content assistant
An agent could examine your previous posts, saved research and current conversations to understand:
Which topics perform best
Which hooks generate the most engagement
What questions your audience repeatedly asks
Which posts deserve a follow-up
What themes you have not covered recently
Which saved ideas could become new content
Then you could prompt it:
“Find the five biggest developments in my niche today and help me with the research to draft original posts”
“Find unanswered questions in my replies and create a content plan”
“Analyze my recent posts and identify the strongest recurring format”
“Draft a thread using only primary sources from the accounts I follow”
With the correct permissions and approval workflow, the same system could prepare and publish content
The important part is that the agent is no longer working from a blank prompt
It is working from your real account history, your research and the live conversation happening on X
3. Automated monitoring
Businesses can use the same infrastructure for much more than content
An agent could monitor:
• Brand mentions
• Product feedback
• Customer complaints
• Competitor announcements
• Industry conversations
• Emerging narratives
• Security incidents
• Service outages
• Regulatory developments
• Relevant journalists, analysts and employees
It could then classify each post by urgency, sentiment, topic or source credibility
A company could ask:
“Show me every serious complaint about our product from the last 24 hours”
“Identify sudden increases in negative discussion”
“Find customers asking for the same missing feature”
“Track what developers are saying about our latest API release”
“Create a daily competitor intelligence report”
This turns X from a passive social feed into a real-time operational data source
4. Organizing your entire information flow
Agents can also help clean and maintain your account
They could:
• Add or remove bookmarks
• Organize bookmarks into folders
• Create curated lists of accounts
• Find duplicate or outdated saved posts
• Separate research from entertainment
• Tag information by project
• Archive completed research
• Build summaries that persist outside X
You could have one folder for AI research, another for design inspiration, one for SpaceX updates and another for business ideas
The agent could continuously organize new bookmarks as you save them instead of allowing the collection to become unmanageable again
5. Audience and community intelligence
Your X activity contains useful signals about your audience
An agent can help analyze:
• Mentions and replies
• Frequently discussed topics
• Highly engaged followers
• Common questions
• Recurring disagreements
• Posts that drive profile visits
• Communities interacting with your content
This does not mean blindly optimizing everything for engagement. It means understanding what people are actually responding to instead of guessing
You could ask:
“Summarize the main arguments people made under this post”
“Identify thoughtful replies that deserve a response”
“Show me the questions that appeared most frequently this week”
“Find experts who consistently contribute useful information”
“Create a report on how my audience’s interests are changing”
That is far more useful than staring at isolated view and like counts
6. Agentic actions, not just analysis
The real shift happens when the agent can act

Through the X API, authorized tools can create or edit posts, manage bookmarks and lists, and interact with user-context endpoints

That means you could build workflows where the agent:
• Conducts research
• Produces a summary
• Drafts the content
• Checks claims against sources
• Requests your approval
• Publishes the final post
• Monitors the response
• Summarizes the conversation afterward
The human still controls the important decisions. But the repetitive work around those decisions can be automated
7. Why MCP makes this easier
X now provides resources for connecting its API to MCP-compatible AI tools
MCP allows an agent to discover and use external tools through a standardized interface
Instead of writing a completely separate integration for every agent, the X API can be exposed as a set of tools that compatible clients understand
Grok Build already supports connecting external MCP servers, which means X tools can sit alongside file access, terminal commands, web search, databases and other production tools
The agent can move between them as part of the same workflow
For example:
“Read my recent bookmarks, research the companies mentioned, compare their latest product announcements, save the findings to a document and draft an X article”
That single request can involve:
• X API access
• Web research
• Local file creation
• Data analysis
• Writing
• Content formatting
This is why agentic tools feel fundamentally different from ordinary chatbots. They do not only answer questions. They can coordinate actions across multiple systems to complete an outcome
8. You still control the permissions
This should be approached carefully
Your agent should only receive the permissions needed for the task
A research agent may only require read access
An agent that manages bookmarks needs bookmark permissions
Posting and account management require additional user-authorized access
A strong setup should begin with read-only permissions and add write access only when necessary
High-impact actions such as publishing posts, deleting content or sending messages should require explicit approval
API credentials should be stored securely and never pasted into public prompts, screenshots or repositories
The goal is not to hand your entire account to an autonomous system without supervision
The goal is to give a capable agent controlled access to useful tools while keeping you in charge
9. The economics are becoming more practical
X now offers reduced pricing for “Owned Reads”......requests involving your own posts, bookmarks, followers, likes and related account data
That makes personal research, organization and automation workflows more practical than treating every request like large-scale public-data collection
You can begin with a narrow workflow, measure its usage and expand only when it provides real value
Start with:
“Summarize my bookmarks”
Then move toward:
“Maintain a living research system built from everything I save on X”
The second workflow is where this becomes genuinely powerful. Your bookmarks stop being a pile of forgotten links. They become long-term memory for your AI agent
Your timeline stops being an endless stream. It becomes a searchable real-time information source
